cases.purpose: 1006 mode on the TTY precedes a consumer read; injected sgr bytes decode to the hand-calculated press and mode is disabled.
cases.script:
saved=$(/bin/stty -g) || exit 21
/bin/stty -icanon -echo min 1 time 0 || exit 22
mouse enable 1006
printf 'READY-READ\n'
IFS= read -r -N 9 report || exit 23
hex=$(printf '%s' "$report" | /usr/bin/od -An -tx1 | /usr/bin/tr -d ' \n')
mouse decode "$hex"
rc=$?
mouse disable 1006
/bin/stty "$saved" || exit 24
exit "$rc"

steps.expect: mouse protocol=1006 kind=press button=button1 x=4 y=6 mods= code=0

cases.oracle: XTerm mouse tracking protocol (SGR 1006, urxvt 1015, legacy X10) and documented mouse record format. Injected input is independently hand-encoded; the consumer is fixture Bash code. This is a byte-stream lifecycle, not a terminal-emulator mode-state assertion.
cases.comparison: The private PTY driver captures raw output, step events and terminal modes with bounded time/output; each fixed contract predicate and natural status is checked independently in both builds.

cases.purpose: The fixture consumer traps Ctrl-C, emits all disable controls, and restores termios.
cases.script:
saved=$(/bin/stty -g) || exit 21
/bin/stty -icanon -echo min 1 time 0 || exit 22
trap 'mouse disable all; /bin/stty "$saved"; printf "\nINT-CLEANED\n"; exit 130' INT
mouse enable all
printf 'READY-INT\n'
IFS= read -r -N 1 unused
exit 25
